query: A TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy has been reported in a single-phase BCC, dendritic state, with a yield strength of about 800 MPa and roughly 40% strain under lower-temperature testing, but at 1273 K it retains only 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain. For its use as an intermediate layer that transfers heat between W and CuCrZr while preserving structural integrity, what single intervention could overcome this loss of strength at elevated temperature? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the reported baseline, define the applicable thermal and mechanical boundary conditions, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic mixtures of high-purity (~99.9%, ~10 µm) Cr, Fe, V, W and either Ta or Ti powders, initially present as separate elemental phases; corresponding equiatomic random atomic configurations were initialized in candidate bcc and fcc simulation cells.
generation.intervention: Classical molecular-dynamics simulations (LAMMPS, embedded-atom-method potential) were used to heat FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles as a function of radius. Constructed radii were reported as 7.5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 Å, although the Results also analyze a 5 Å particle.
generation.conditions: Simulations used periodic boundaries, an NPT ensemble at 1 atm, EAM/MIE interaction potentials, 4394 atoms for bcc or 4000 atoms for fcc cells, 6×10^6 time steps, and in hybrid MC an attempted unlike-atom swap every 10 MD steps over temperatures including 300–2100 K. SPS was performed for 5 min at 1543 K/70 MPa, with CrFeTaVW also processed under vacuum at 1573 K/80 MPa. Laser-flash thermal diffusivity was measured under 0.05 bar He from 300 to 1000 K.
generation.structural_mediator: Mechanical alloying produced bcc-type solid solutions in both powders. After SPS, CrFeTaVW retained a bcc matrix (a≈0.312 nm) but also formed an Fe2Ta C14 Laves phase and V- and W-rich regions; CrFeTiVW exhibited two bcc-derived structures (a≈0.310 and 0.298 nm) with Ti- and W-rich regions. A body-centered-tetragonal distortion is only proposed as an alternative interpretation for CrFeTiVW and requires further crystallographic confirmation. Atomic-scale disorder and temperature-dependent lattice expansion mediate thermal transport.
generation.mechanism: Hybrid MC swaps seek thermodynamically lower-energy chemical arrangements and produced lower potential energies than MD. MC predicted enhanced W–W association and segregation in CrFeTiVW, especially around 1200 K, whereas segregation was less pronounced for CrFeTaVW. Strongly negative Fe–Ta mixing enthalpy and atomic-size mismatch favor Fe2Ta Laves-phase formation during consolidation. For thermal transport, multielement disorder shortens the phonon mean free path and lowers diffusivity relative to W and CuCrZr, while lattice expansion at increasing temperature lengthens the mean free path and causes a modest diffusivity rise. Similar Ta and Ti atomic radii make their substitution have little effect on diffusivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to conventional MD, hybrid MC was expected to yield lower-energy, more stable configurations and to discriminate alloy-specific segregation, with stronger W-related segregation in CrFeTiVW than in CrFeTaVW. Relative to the unmilled elemental mixtures, milling and SPS were expected to produce predominantly bcc-derived HEA structures. Replacing Ta with Ti was predicted to alter the consolidated phase constitution—from bcc plus a Laves phase to two bcc-derived phases—without materially changing thermal diffusivity; both alloys were expected to have much lower diffusivity than pure W or CuCrZr.
generation.baseline: The principal computational baseline was conventional MD without MC atom swaps. Experimental baselines included the unmilled elemental powder mixtures, CrFeTaVW as the composition before Ta-to-Ti substitution, and pure W/CuCrZr or literature HEAs as thermal-diffusivity references.
generation.boundary: The conclusions apply to equiatomic CrFeTaVW and CrFeTiVW under the specified potential models, simulated temperatures and NPT conditions, and to ball-milled/SPS-consolidated specimens tested from 300 to 1000 K. Simulated segregation is a qualitative equilibrium tendency because MC swaps omit real diffusion kinetics; rapid SPS, cooling, contamination, and other nonequilibrium effects can generate experimental phases or segregation not reproduced by simulation. The proposed bct interpretation of CrFeTiVW remains unconfirmed.

falsification_experiment.design: Potential energy versus temperature, local-composition standard deviation across 27 sampling regions, simulated atomic configurations, partial radial distribution functions and W–W bond probability discriminated MD from MC predictions. Powder X-ray diffraction identified phase constitution and lattice parameters; SEM/BSE with EDS maps tested elemental segregation and microstructure; laser-flash measurements determined thermal diffusivity versus temperature.
measurements: Potential energy versus temperature, local-composition standard deviation across 27 sampling regions, simulated atomic configurations, partial radial distribution functions and W–W bond probability discriminated MD from MC predictions. Powder X-ray diffraction identified phase constitution and lattice parameters; SEM/BSE with EDS maps tested elemental segregation and microstructure; laser-flash measurements determined thermal diffusivity versus temperature.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
